title_en: The Fungus That Turns Ants into Zombies
english_paragraphs: Deep in a Thai rainforest, a carpenter ant breaks from its colony's column in the lofty canopy. Swaying on unsteady legs, it wanders downward, as if intoxicated, into leafy undergrowth. Around midday it clenches its jaws on a major vein underneath a leaf, about 25 centimetres above the ground.

By dusk the insect is lifeless, yet the bite holds rigidly. A fungus has destroyed its jaw muscles, so they cannot loosen. Two or three days later a fungal stalk pushes from its head and releases infectious spores on to the ground below, where foraging ants tread.

The invader, Ophiocordyceps unilateralis, is fussy about location. David Hughes and colleagues found the bites mostly on the north-west side of plants, where the air is humid and the temperature suits the fungus. When researchers moved infected ants higher, the fungus grew abnormally. Placed on the ground, the bodies disappeared.

In 2017 a Penn State team examined infected ants with three-dimensional microscope imaging. Fungal cells had formed an intertwined lattice around muscle fibres in the legs and jaw, a picture that evokes the strings of a puppet. Yet the fungus had not infiltrated the brain.

A Planet Earth episode, with David Attenborough's narration, showed one such ant. It helped inspire The Last of Us, a 2013 video game whose makers envisioned the parasite jumping to humans. The hypothetical scenario gave gamers a fictional nightmare.
The real parasite's roots run far deeper, into the geological record. A 48-million-year-old fossil leaf from Messel, in Germany, bears the same characteristic bite scars.
chinese_source_paragraphs: 在泰国**雨林**(rainforest)深处，一只**木匠**(carpenter)蚁脱离了它的蚁**群**(colony)**队列**(column)，在**高耸的**(lofty)**树冠**(canopy)上（前行）。**摇摇晃晃**(Swaying)，腿脚**不稳**(unsteady)，它**向下**(downward)**游荡**(wanders)，**好像**(as if)**喝醉了**(intoxicated)一样，进入**枝叶茂密的**(leafy)**林下植被**(undergrowth)。**正午**(midday)前后，它将**双颚**(jaws)**紧咬**(clenches)在一片叶子下方的一条主**叶脉**(vein)上，离地面约25厘米。
到**黄昏**(dusk)时，这只昆虫已**无生命**(lifeless)，那一口却仍**牢牢地**(rigidly)咬着。一种真菌摧毁了它的颚部**肌肉**(muscles)，因此它们无法**松开**(loosen)。两三天后，一根**真菌**(fungal)菌柄从它头部顶出，将**具有传染性的**(infectious)孢子释放到下方的地面上，那里有觅食的蚂蚁**行走**(tread)。

这个**入侵者**(invader)，也就是偏侧蛇虫草菌，对**位置**(location)很**挑剔**(fussy)。戴维·休斯和同事发现，这些**咬合点**(bites)大多在植物的**西北**(north-west)侧，那里空气**潮湿**(humid)，且温度适宜真菌。研究人员把受感染的蚂蚁移到更高处时，真菌长得很**反常**(abnormally)。放在地面上，尸体则**不见了**(disappeared)。

2017年，宾夕法尼亚州立大学的一个团队检查了受感染的蚂蚁，用的是**三维**(three-dimensional)**显微镜**(microscope)成像。真菌细胞形成了**相互交织的**(intertwined)**网格**(lattice)，围在腿部和颚部的肌肉纤维周围，一幅**使人想起**(evokes)**木偶**(puppet)的提线的画面。不过，真菌尚未**渗入**(infiltrated)大脑。

《地球脉动》的一集，伴随着戴维·阿滕伯勒的**解说**(narration)，就展示了这样一只蚂蚁。它帮助**启发了**(inspire)2013年的电子游戏《最后生还者》，游戏的**制作者**(makers)们**设想**(envisioned)这种寄生菌跳到了人类身上。这个**假想的**(hypothetical)**情景**(scenario)给**玩家**(gamers)带来了一场**虚构的**(fictional)噩梦。
现实中的寄生菌，其根源要深得多，一直延伸到**地质**(geological)记录之中。一片4800万年前的叶子**化石**(fossil)，出土于德国梅塞尔，上面带有同样**典型的**(characteristic)咬合**疤痕**(scars)。
